resources.string: F13 (a dedicated key sent from QMK, etc.)
Choose the keys to use with a US layout. On a JIS layout, Henkan (on), Muhenkan (off), Kana (on), and Hankaku/Zenkaku (toggle) always work.
Type numbers and symbols in full width
When off, they are typed in half width. Both appear as conversion candidates.
Typing 「 or （ also inserts the closing bracket and puts the cursor inside. Pressing Space on empty brackets cycles through 「」『』【】 and more.
Shows the converted result as you type.
Shows words that complete what you are typing (きーぼ → キーボード) in the candidate window. Tap one, or choose with Tab and press Enter.
Candidates you picked before appear higher next time.
Deletes all learned candidates. Your user dictionary is kept.
The on-screen keyboard is used when no physical keyboard is connected.
Shows only when there is no physical keyboard.
Shows even when a physical keyboard is connected.
Swipe up on the bottom-left key (?123 on Glide, Ctrl on Full keyboard, “あa1” on 12-key) to switch to the next of your enabled layouts.
Layouts to use (the bottom-left key cycles only through these)
Slide your finger over the QWERTY letter keys to enter a word. For Japanese, slide through the romaji to get kana. Numbers and symbols are on the ?123 page.
Swipe a key to get numbers and symbols. Ctrl, Alt, Fn, Esc, and Tab are also there, so you can use it like a physical keyboard.
Type on 12 keys by flicking (toggle input is also available).

For Japanese glide typing, zenz (the language model used to reorder conversions) checks how the word fits with the preceding text. The top dictionary match is entered first, and if zenz picks a different word, it is swapped in shortly after.
Pressing the same key repeatedly moves to the next character (あ→い→う). When off, only flicks are used.

Swipe down on the あ/A key (on the keypad, swipe ☺; on a physical keyboard, press the shortcut below) to see the history of copied text and images. Tap to paste; long-press to pin, edit, crop, or delete. Each card shows the app the keyboard was connected to when you copied. Copies marked as sensitive, such as passwords, are not kept.

With a physical keyboard connected, this shortcut opens the same clipboard as the on-screen keyboard, near the cursor. Choose with the arrow keys or Tab and press Enter, or press a number to paste; Esc closes it. With Ctrl+Shift+V, it opens instead of the app\'s \"paste as plain text\".
Press a key combination on the physical keyboard to use it (with Ctrl, Shift, Alt, or Meta). You can also pick from the list. Combinations the device takes first (such as Meta+V) may not work.
Items older than this are deleted automatically. Pinned items are kept.
If the keyboard overlaps the navigation bar, increase the bottom margin. Changes apply the next time the keyboard opens.
• Swipe a key toward a corner or edge to get the small character (number or symbol) printed on it.
• Shift, Ctrl, Alt, and Fn apply to the next key only; press twice to lock. You can also hold one while pressing another key.
• Modifier presses and releases are sent too, so Shift+arrow selection and app shortcuts work just like on a physical keyboard.
• Swipe up on Alt for Meta (⌘). Fn+number enters F1–F10, and Fn+- = enters F11 and F12.
• Swipe Space left or right for arrow keys. Swipe the Tab key in a direction for arrow keys, or toward a corner for Home, End, PgUp, and PgDn. Swipe Backspace right for Delete.
• The mic key records only while held. A short press keeps listening.
Apps that show typing in the bar
In apps that can\'t display text being typed (terminal apps such as Termux), the text being typed is shown in the bar instead.
Text being typed will no longer be shown in the bar for this app.
Search by name or package name

Register readings and words. Registered words are preferred in conversion and appear first in the candidates, marked \"User dictionary\" (like the macOS user dictionary). They are also more likely to be used for that reading in the middle of a sentence.
Write \"reading word\" on each line (split at the first space). Lines starting with # are ignored.

As soon as you finish typing a key, it is replaced with the output (e.g. @@ → email address, -> → →). Works both in Japanese input and direct input. The key is matched against the characters you actually type (before they become kana or full width). Keys of only letters also react to romaji, so keys that include symbols are recommended. Longer keys take priority.
Write \"key output\" on each line (split at the first space). \\n in the output is a line break. Lines starting with # are ignored.
%1$s You can write everything at once in an editor, or copy from here to export.
How far you must move your finger (as a share of the key width) before a touch counts as a swipe for numbers and symbols. Raise it if you often get symbols when you meant to type letters.

On the Glide and 12-key layouts, when you tap near the edge between keys, Kanade picks the key whose character is more likely to come next in the word you\'re typing. Taps near the middle of a key are never changed.
Scores the top 10 dictionary conversions with zenz and reorders them.
Like azooKey\'s Zenzai: zenz checks the top dictionary conversion and, where it disagrees, the dictionary searches again from that point. About as accurate as reranking with far less computation.
Tells zenz about you so it can choose fitting words (up to 25 characters, %1$d used). Leave empty to not use it.
